chunks: And Abān ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Four things are not permissible in four situations: treachery, embezzlement, theft, and usury. They are not permissible in hajj, nor ʿumrah, nor jihad, nor charity."

key_terms.الْغُلُولُ: embezzlement or misappropriation, especially from entrusted property
key_terms.جِهَادٍ: jihad; striving in the path of Allah
key_terms.حَجٍّ: hajj; the pilgrimage to the Sacred House

ai.seo_question: Can treachery, theft, or usury ever be justified in hajj, ʿumrah, jihad, or charity?
ai.summary: This hadith states that certain unlawful financial and moral violations remain forbidden even when associated with outwardly righteous acts. It emphasizes that acts such as hajj, ʿumrah, jihad, and charity are not validly accompanied by treachery, misappropriation, theft, or usury.
